about.title: Folsom Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Six people died on Folsom's roads in 2025, the city's most recent final count. Behind that figure are households near E Bidwell Street, Iron Point Road, Blue Ravine Road and Riley Street that are now arranging services instead of weeknight dinners. If that describes your family, we are sorry you are reading this. A wrongful death claim in Sacramento County is a civil matter, kept entirely apart from anything the district attorney may pursue. Its purpose is practical: to recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. California limits who may bring the case. A spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The filing deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and it shrinks considerably when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that pairs Folsom families with an independent attorney who works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Folsom Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California gives standing first to a spouse or domestic partner and children, then to certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can sort out quickly whether you qualify and who else should be part of the claim.

items.title: The two-year clock is watched closely
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is much shorter when a city, county or state agency may share fault. Early attention protects your options.

items.title: Every category of loss is counted
items.desc: Funeral and burial expenses, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance are all recoverable under California law. Your attorney handles the case on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on Blue Ravine Road. Does the criminal case decide our claim?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death case is a civil action that runs on its own track, separate from any charges the Sacramento County District Attorney files. The civil claim has a different standard of proof and a different goal, which is compensating your family rather than punishing the driver. You can pursue it whether or not criminal charges are ever brought.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The law puts the surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children first in line. If there are none, certain dependents and heirs may qualify instead. Because the rules can affect parents, stepchildren and financially dependent relatives differently, an attorney should review your specific family situation before anything is filed.

items.question: How long do we have to act, and does it matter if a Folsom city vehicle or road condition was involved?
items.answer: In most cases the deadline is two years from the date of death. If a government entity may be responsible, such as a city or county, a formal claim must be presented within a much shorter period before a lawsuit can proceed. Reaching out sooner rather than later helps keep every path open for your family.
